The diagram shows a production possibility curve (PPC) for an economy that can produce cotton and cars. The economy is at point Q. There is improved technology that can only be used in the production of cars. How would this be represented on this diagram?
image: A production possibility curve (PPC) diagram with 'output of cotton' on the vertical axis and 'output of cars' on the horizontal axis. The curve shows a bowed-out shape, originating near the vertical axis and ending on the horizontal axis. Points Z, Q, and Y are located on the curve from top-left to bottom-right. Point W is located outside and above the curve, towards the top-right. Point X is located inside the curve, below and to the left of point Q. The PPC itself represents the maximum possible combinations of cotton and cars given existing resources and technology.
